name: Pancreatic cancer
theme: the resectability fork · the pan-RAS turn

meta.title: Pancreatic cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma - the registry's four-way fork: everything downstream hangs on the resectability read (resectable / borderline resectable / locally advanced / metastatic), an anatomic judgment made at a scanner and confirmed at a tumor board, not a lab value. Adenosquamous and acinar variants ride inside with a note (the modern trials largely enrolled PDAC; RASolute 303 explicitly allows adenosquamous). Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors are a different disease with their own row; ampullary and bile-duct primaries belong to the biliary row - both rerouted. Two universal tests run under everything: germline testing for every patient (BRCA1/2, PALB2, ATM - the ASCO provisional clinical opinion), and somatic NGS with RNA fusion detection - because the ~10% KRAS wild-type minority is where the rare tickets (NRG1, MSI-H) hide. And 2026 is the year this disease's ledger turned: the first pan-RAS inhibitor doubled second-line survival in a phase 3 - positive, plenary, published, and honestly NOT yet approved.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease where the resectability fork picks the menu and 2026 moved the ceiling. Resectable: upfront surgery then adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX holds the anchor (PRODIGE-24: 5-year OS 43.2% vs 31.4%, median 53.5 vs 35.5 - the mature update), and the trainer keeps the neoadjuvant honesty visible: NORPACT-1 was NEGATIVE for neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX in resectable disease, and Alliance A021806 has NOT read out (accrual complete, primary completion 2028) - the perioperative question is open, not answered. Borderline: neoadjuvant first is the proven sequence (PREOPA…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: AJCC 8th edition TNM (v9 released for pancreatic NET, NOT yet for exocrine PDAC - flagged secondhand); NCCN anatomic resectability definitions (SMV/PV, SMA/CA/CHA involvement - secondhand, 403); CA 19-9 as marker with the Lewis-null non-secretor caveat
meta.response: RECIST 1.1; the load-bearing reads are the post-induction restaging (the consolidation/maintenance/conversion fork) and CA 19-9 kinetics alongside it

Newly diagnosed.name: Upfront resection -> adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX (PRODIGE-24 - the anchor)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized with 5-year maturity (PRODIGE-24); the perioperative alternative unproven (A021806 unread)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a major operation, then six months of triplet chemotherapy - the hardest curative road in this registry, walked for the only real cure fraction
Newly diagnosed.patient: When an operation is possible: surgery first, then six months of strong chemotherapy - the combination that produced the best long-term numbers this disease has, with four in ten patients alive at five years in the key trial.

Newly diagnosed.name: Neoadjuvant therapy -> surgery (PREOPANC - borderline's proven sequence)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: neoadjuvant-first for borderline (NCCN, secondhand; PREOPANC randomized basis)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized (PREOPANC long-term; PREOPANC-2 equivalence) - subgroup percentages flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: months of chemotherapy (or chemoradiation) before knowing whether the operation happens - the psychological weight is named, not minimized
Newly diagnosed.patient: When the tumor touches key blood vessels: treatment first, operation second - the order that proved better for exactly this situation, with two regimen choices shown to work equally well.

Newly diagnosed.name: Induction chemotherapy (locally advanced - consolidation is a trial question)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: induction-first (NCCN, secondhand); consolidative CRT not survival-proven (LAP07)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized (LAP07 - the honest negative); ablative-RT question open (LAP100)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the long chemotherapy road with an unresolved consolidation question at the end of it - stated as such
Newly diagnosed.patient: When the tumor is wrapped around vessels but has not spread: months of chemotherapy to hold and shrink it - with radiation afterward an honest open question (the old trial showed no survival gain; a new one is testing a much stronger technique).

Newly diagnosed.name: FOLFIRINOX or NALIRIFOX (fit metastatic 1L)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - OS met in both
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the triplet ledger: cytopenias, diarrhea, neuropathy - bought against the doublet's gentler road with the honest arithmetic shown
Newly diagnosed.patient: For spread disease with good strength: the three-drug combinations - the strongest proven openers, adding months of survival over older treatment.

Newly diagnosed.name: Gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel (MPACT - the broader-shoulders road)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN 1L across a broader fitness range (secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: gentler than the triplets and honest about it: cytopenias, neuropathy, fatigue - the trade the co-display exists to show
Newly diagnosed.patient: The two-drug option: real proven benefit with a lighter load - often the honest choice when strength is limited.

Newly diagnosed.name: Maintenance olaparib (POLO - the germline ticket's payoff, both halves said)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: FDA-approved maintenance for gBRCA metastatic PDAC (date secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met; OS NS (both halves on the card)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: tablet-road anemia and fatigue - traded for a chemotherapy holiday, which is the honest unit of benefit here
Newly diagnosed.patient: For people with the inherited BRCA-type change whose chemo is holding: a tablet can hold the line longer without chemotherapy - it roughly doubled the held time, though it has not been shown to extend life overall, and the card says both.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; biliary plumbing, digestion, and pain control are the craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining chemotherapy is a real choice - and in this disease comfort care is still active care: stents for jaundice, enzymes for digestion, real pain expertise.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Daraxonrasib (RASolute 302 - the pan-RAS turn: positive, published, NOT yet approved)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FDA-APPROVED 2026-08-26 (RASONQUE; FDA approval notice, firsthand 2026-09-07); EAP record NCT07573215 flipped to APPROVED_FOR_MARKETING - g…
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - OS HR 0.40, plenary + NEJM (PMID pending capture); regulatory decision pending
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: rash, GI effects, and the oral-targeted ledger - measurably gentler than the chemotherapy it beat
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The newest chapter: a tablet targeting this cancer's central mutation doubled survival after chemotherapy stopped working - in a proper randomized trial. It is not yet approved; today it is reached through a special access program or a trial, and this card will change the week that changes.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Nal-IRI + 5FU/LV (NAPOLI-1 - the proven 2L spine)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: diarrhea and cytopenias - the irinotecan ledger, familiar and managed
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The proven second chemotherapy: a modest, real benefit - and the honest yardstick the newest tablet is measured against.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Sotorasib (KRAS G12C - the rare ticket, labeled)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: off-label/compendia territory (secondhand); olomorasib BTD 2026-08 - not approved
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: diarrhea and hepatotoxicity watch - the G12C-inhibitor signature
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the rare G12C version of the mutation: a targeted tablet shrinks about one tumor in five - modest, real, and shown here with its early-evidence label; a newer cousin drug just earned fast-track status.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Zenocutuzumab (NRG1 fusion - the RNA-seq ticket, approved)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: infusion reactions and GI effects - generally gentle for what it does
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the rare NRG1 fusion (found only if the tumor's RNA was tested): an approved antibody shrinks about four in ten of these cancers - the best argument in this disease for complete molecular testing.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pembrolizumab (MSI-H - tumor-agnostic, with the pancreatic caveat)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the immune ledger - and honest expectations, per the caveat
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the rare immune-visible version of this cancer: immunotherapy can produce lasting responses - though pancreatic cancers respond less often than the average across cancer types, and the card says so.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged); randomized control-arm bracket verified
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after progression is a real road - with a team whose whole craft is digestion, pain, and good days.

Wainberg et al. NAPOLI-3: NALIRIFOX vs gem-nab-P, 1L metastatic - OS 11.1 vs 9.2 (HR 0.83, p=0.036), PFS 7.4 vs 5.6; FDA approved 2024-02-13 (date secondhand). Lancet 2023;402:1272-81 (PMID 37708904, verified)

Golan et al. POLO final OS: 19.0 vs 19.2 months, NOT significant (HR 0.83, p=0.35); 3-yr OS 33.9% vs 17.8% (tail signal, not a claim) - the other half, said aloud. JCO 2022;40:3929-39 (PMID 35834777, verified)

Wang-Gillam et al. NAPOLI-1: nal-IRI + 5FU/LV post-gemcitabine - OS 6.1 vs 4.2 (HR 0.67, p=0.012) - the proven 2L spine and the bar the pan-RAS card is measured against. Lancet 2016;387:545-57 (PMID 26615328, verified)

RASolute 302 (NCT06625320): daraxonrasib (pan-RAS(ON)) vs SOC chemo, previously treated metastatic PDAC - median OS 13.2 vs 6.6 (RAS G12 population; HR 0.40, p<0.0001; overall 13.2 vs 6.7, HR 0.40), grade >=3 adverse events (ALL-CAUSE, as the paper reports them) 61.8% vs 69.6%, and treatment-related events leading to discontinuation 1.2% vs 11.2%; PFS 7.3 vs 3.5 mo (RAS G12, HR 0.45) and 7.2 vs 3.6 overall (HR 0.49). Abstract re-read firsthand 2026-09-10; the previously displayed 'grade >=3 TRAEs 43.6% vs 57.5%' appears nowhere in the publication and the direction-of-benefit claim it supported now rests on 61.8% vs 69.6%. ASCO 2026 plenary (LBA5); O'Reilly EM et al. N Engl J Med 2026;395(4):325-337 (PMID 42223072, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2605555) - PMID captured 2026-09-07

Daraxonrasib regulatory state as of 2026-09-07: FDA-APPROVED 2026-08-26 as RASONQUE (regular approval, Real-Time Oncology Review; Breakthrough + Orphan; CNPV pilot participant) for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma after >=1 prior systemic therapy or not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy, 300 mg PO once daily. FDA-cited efficacy (overall population): OS 13.2 vs 6.7 (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.30-0.53), PFS 7.2 vs 3.6, ORR 30% vs 11%. EAP NCT07573215 now APPROVED_FOR_MARKETING. Watch item CLOSED - NCCN inclusion is the next watch

Strickler et al. Sotorasib in KRAS G12C pancreatic cancer (CodeBreaK 100 cohort): ORR 21%, PFS 4.0, OS 6.9. NEJM 2023;388:33-43 (PMID 36546651, verified - wrong-PMID catch #21: the near-miss candidate 36546661 resolves to a COVID neutralization letter)

Olomorasib: FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation 2026-08-03 for previously treated KRAS G12C-mutant advanced pancreatic cancer (LOXO-RAS-20001, NCT04956640) - designation, NOT approval; secondhand (sponsor announcement)

Marabelle et al. KEYNOTE-158: pembrolizumab in noncolorectal MSI-H tumors - ORR 34.3% across the basket; pancreatic-cohort responses run LOWER in cohort analyses (caveat flagged on the card). JCO 2020;38:1-10 (PMID 31682550, verified)
Schram et al. eNRGy: zenocutuzumab in NRG1 fusion-positive cancers - ORR 30% overall; PANCREATIC 15/36 = 42%. NEJM 2025;392:566-76 (PMID 39908431, verified)

FDA: accelerated approval of zenocutuzumab-zbco (Bizengri) 2024-12-04 for NRG1+ NSCLC and NRG1+ pancreatic adenocarcinoma post-progression - the one PRIMARY-VERIFIED FDA approval in this spec (fda.gov announcement)

Stoffel et al. ASCO Provisional Clinical Opinion: germline testing discussed with ALL pancreatic adenocarcinoma patients regardless of family history (BRCA1/2, PALB2, ATM et al). JCO 2019;37:153-64 (PMID 30457921, verified)

Dominguez-Munoz et al. European guidelines (UEG/EPC/ESPEN et al) for pancreatic exocrine insufficiency: PERT indicated in PEI from pancreatic disease and surgery, explicitly incl. pancreatic cancer - the verified supportive-spine anchor. United European Gastroenterol J 2025;13:125-72 (PMID 39639485, verified)

ELI-002 7P AMPLIFY-7P (NCT05726864): phase 2 adjuvant KRAS-directed vaccine - enrollment completed 2024-12; June 2026 readout MISSED the primary DFS endpoint in ITT; sponsor pivoting to a refined phase 3 strategy. ACTIVE NOT RECRUITING - excluded from the open list, kept as the vaccine ledger's honest first verdict (sponsor announcement)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

RASolute 303 (NCT07491445): daraxonrasib mono or + gem-nab-P vs gem-nab-P, 1L metastatic PDAC, ANY documented RAS status (mutant and wild-type eligible), n=900, phase 3 3-arm, dual PFS/OS primaries, 14 US sites recruiting - registry-verified 2026-08. Sibling RASolute 305 (NCT07621718): zoldonrasib + chemo vs chemo, KRAS G12D-gated, n=670, recruiting (5 US sites, early rollout). MRTX1133 (G12D pioneer): TERMINATED

RASolute 304 (NCT07252232): adjuvant daraxonrasib vs observation after completed perioperative chemo, resected RAS-mutant PDAC, n=500, phase 3, DFS primary, 33 US sites (~32 recruiting) - registry-verified 2026-08

NRG LAP100 (NCT06958328): ablative dose-escalated RT vs continued systemic therapy in locally advanced PDAC held through 4-6 months induction with CA 19-9 response, n=356, phase 3, OS primary, 322 sites, ECOG 0-2 - registry-verified 2026-08

IMCODE003 (NCT05968326): adjuvant autogene cevumeran (individualized mRNA neoantigen vaccine) + atezolizumab + mFOLFIRINOX vs mFOLFIRINOX, resected treatment-naive PDAC, n=260, randomized phase 2, DFS primary, ~31 US sites recruiting (Genentech/BioNTech) - registry-verified 2026-08

APOLLO (NCT04858334): maintenance olaparib vs placebo after curative-intent therapy, germline OR somatic BRCA1/2/PALB2, n=152, randomized phase 2 double-blind, RFS primary, 454 sites (NCI/ECOG-ACRIN - the widest footprint on this screen), ECOG 0-2 - registry-verified 2026-08

SWOG (NCT06998940): 2L chemotherapy +/- panitumumab, KRAS AND BRAF wild-type by tissue NGS (ctDNA not accepted), locally advanced/metastatic PDAC, n=94, phase 3, OS primary, 274 sites, ECOG 0-2 - registry-verified 2026-08
